messages:
Rina: Opening thread for a weird onboarding hiccup on brontide-30k-int4. Observed reproducible token boundary slips when kv-prefetch + dynamic-rope-scaling are both enabled.

Rina: Repro command: `./local_infer --model brontide-30k-int4 --quant=int4 --kv-prefetch=on --rope-mode=dynamic --ctx=32768 --prompt=tests/long_seed.txt`

Rina: Fail pattern: around ~13,712 tokens we see a consistent subword split and punctuation detach. Happens across runs on same node.

telemetry-bot: Trace: https://telemetry.internal/trace/1819992222 (ttl 7d)

Marco: Can you paste a short log? Specifically interested in rope_scale values around that pos and kv read/write indices.

Rina: Log excerpt: `pos=13712 rope_scale=0.999842 frac=0.413402 kv_write=13711 kv_read=13713` (expected read==write or write+1 depending on policy but not +2)

Ivy: Curious if this is tied to quantized scale math. int4 reduces precision and we do per-shard float reductions in the prefill path. Did you run single-shard and multi-shard to compare?

Rina: Single-shard reproduces. Multi-shard showed same symptom but at slightly different pos (13710 / 13712). So sharding changes the breakpoint, but not the root.

Sam: My take: dynamic rope scaling computes a per-position multiplier using trig interpolation. Small fp differences -> when multiplied by large pos can produce a different rounded kv index. Over the prefetch horizon these tiny diffs accumulate and produce a slip at boundaries.

Marco: Two quick experiments: 1) replace float scaling with fixedpoint (scale_i = round(scale*2**16)) and recompute kv_idx via integer math; 2) increase quantization bits for scale (simulate higher precision) and see if it moves the breakpoint.

Ivy: Also try disabling `kv_prefetch` and confirm symptom disappears to ensure prefetch window logic interacts here.

Rina: Confirmed: `--kv-prefetch=off` removes slip. Also `--rope-mode=linear` removes slip with prefetch on. So it's interaction of dynamic schedule + prefetch.

Sam: I wrote a tiny proof-of-concept where scale is stored as int32 fixedpoint with N=20. Re-running reproducer: slip disappears in my quick run. I'll push patch to my branch for CI fuzz.

telemetry-bot: Brontide run traces and small kv dumps uploaded: https://telemetry.internal/dumps/1819992222/ (ttl 7d)

Marco: Nice. Please add a microbenchmark measuring overhead of fixedpoint mapping on prefill CPU time. We need to ensure we aren't regressing throughput.

Sam: Microbench: added mapping_time_us metric. Fixedpoint adds ~0.4us/token in prefill stage on x86_64, negligible vs model time. I'll include numbers in PR.

Ivy: One more angle: rounding rule. If runtime uses `round()` (ties to nearest away) vs bankers rounding, bias could be directional. Try round-to-even in float path as a cheaper experiment.

Sam: Will test both. If round-to-even fixes some cases but not all, fixedpoint seems most robust.

Rina: Also found that when we serialize rope scales to JSON for multi-node prefill, pretty-printing trimmed decimals in one language binding caused tiny deltas and made divergences more frequent. Binary serialization avoided that.

Marco: Good catch. For sharded workflows we should require canonical on-wire representation (fixedpoint or binary) to prevent cross-language non-determinism. Add that to onboarding checklist for now.

Ivy: I'll add a fuzzbench matrix: brontide-30k-int4 int3/int4, rope-mode dynamic/linear, kv-prefetch horizons 2048/4096/8192, mapping float-fixed/even/fixedpoint. Schedule it for overnight.

build-bot: Fuzz job scheduled: fuzz-1819993000 (24 runs). Link: https://telemetry.internal/fuzz/fuzz-1819993000

Sam: Opening a small PR with: fixedpoint mapping optional flag `--rope-mapping=fixedpoint|float`, round-to-even toggle `--rope-rounding=even|away`, and a note in the onboarding doc. Assigning to Marco for review.

Rina: If fixedpoint looks stable in fuzz, prefer opt-in canary then make default for new model onboardings. For hosted customers, we may need to keep float mapping but guard with canaries.

Marco: Agreed. I'll review PR and run the perf microbench in CI. Also add unit tests that compare kv_idx parity across serialization roundtrips and across little/big-endian to avoid platform surprises.

Ivy: After fuzz completes I'll post aggregate diffs. If any diff remains we should capture exact pos and kv_index table slice for postmortem.

Rina: Thanks team. Prioritizing P2. Leaving traces and dumps in telemetry link above. Will update with fuzz results later. :coffee:
